title: Longest Substring Of All Vowels in Order
statement:
Call a string **beautiful** when it contains each of the five vowels `'a'`, `'e'`, `'i'`, `'o'`, `'u'` at least once and its letters appear in alphabetical order (every `'a'` comes before every `'e'`, every `'e'` before every `'i'`, and so on). For example `"aeiou"` and `"aaeiiioouuu"` are beautiful, while `"aeoiu"` (out of order) and `"aaeeiioo"` (no `'u'`) are not.

The string `word` is made only of vowels. Return the length of the longest contiguous substring of `word` that is beautiful, or `0` if none of its substrings is beautiful.
constraints: word contains only the characters 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o' and 'u'
notes:
## Intuition

A beautiful substring never steps down: each letter is the same as the previous one or a later vowel. So a window can grow to the right as long as the letters do not decrease, and it must restart the moment a letter is smaller than the one before it. Within one non-decreasing window, the letters are all five vowels exactly when the letter has gone up four times starting from `'a'`. Checking every substring would cost O(n²) or worse; one sweep is enough.

## Approach

1. Keep a window `[left, right]` whose letters never decrease, and `distinct`, how many different vowels it holds.
2. For each new `right`: if `word[right]` is smaller than the letter before it, the order breaks, so restart the window at `right` with `distinct = 1`.
3. Otherwise, if it is larger, a new vowel has joined: increase `distinct`.
4. When `distinct === 5`, the window holds `a, e, i, o, u` in order, so update `best` with its length.

## Example 1, step by step

In `"aeiaaioaaaaeiiiiouuuooaauuaeiu"` the window restarts at index 3 (`'a'` after `'i'`) and index 7 (`'a'` after `'o'`). From index 7 the letters `aaaa e iiii o uuu` climb through all five vowels, reaching `distinct = 5` at index 17; the window keeps growing until index 19, giving `best = 19 - 7 + 1 = 13`. The `'o'` at index 20 restarts the window, and no later window reaches five vowels, so the answer is `13`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is compared with its neighbour once.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Five distinct letters only prove a beautiful window because the window never decreases; with a restart on every drop, `distinct = 5` forces the run to begin at `'a'`.
- Restart at `right` itself, not at `right + 1`: the smaller letter may be the `'a'` that starts the next answer.
- A run that reaches `'u'` can keep growing with more `'u'`s; update `best` on every step, not only when `distinct` first becomes 5.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left`, `right` | ends of the current non-decreasing window |
| `distinct` | number of different vowels in the window |
| `best` | longest beautiful window seen so far |

narration.2: No beautiful substring has been seen yet.
narration.3: The first window starts at index 0...
narration.5: Grow the window one character at a time.
narration.6: A letter smaller than its neighbour breaks the alphabetical order.
narration.7: Start a fresh window at this character.
narration.8: The new window holds just this one vowel.
narration.9: A strictly larger letter means a new vowel joined the window.
narration.12: All five vowels in order: this window is beautiful.
narration.16: Return the longest beautiful length, or 0 if no window reached five vowels.
